issues.description: This image has no description for people who cannot see it. [SYSTEMIC PATTERN] This issue appears in 3+ elements, indicating a missing global rule in the design system or CSS framework.
issues.suggestion: Add a short, meaningful description of what the image shows.
issues.description_technical: The element is missing the alt attribute, violating WCAG 2.2 SC 1.1.1 (Non-text Content).
issues.why_simple: A blind user relying on a screen reader hears nothing when this image is reached and loses the information it conveys.
issues.why_technical: Screen readers expose the alt attribute as the accessible name of the img element; without it, the AT announces the filename or 'image', providing no semantic value. NVDA + Firefox: announces 'image' with no label; JAWS 2024: announces 'graphic' with no description.
issues.suggestion_technical: Add alt="" to the element, or alt="" if the image is purely decorative.

issues.description: The alt text is a filename, not a description of the image content.
issues.suggestion: Replace the alt text with a meaningful description of the image.
issues.description_technical: The alt attribute value is 'icecream.jpg ', which is a filename and does not describe the image content, violating WCAG 2.2 SC 1.1.1 (Non-text Content).
issues.why_simple: A screen reader user hears 'icecream.jpg' which gives no information about what the image actually shows.
issues.why_technical: Screen readers announce the alt attribute value as the accessible name; a filename provides no semantic information about the image content. NVDA + Firefox: announces 'icecream.jpg' verbatim; JAWS 2024: announces 'icecream.jpg' with no context.
issues.suggestion_technical: Change alt="icecream.jpg " to alt="<descriptive text>" that accurately describes the image content.

issues.element: <svg height="100%" version="1.1" viewbox="0 0 36 36" width="100%"><!-- SVG desenho omitido --></svg>
issues.description: This SVG is used as meaningful content but has no accessible name.
issues.suggestion: Add an accessible name to the SVG using aria-label or a title element.
issues.description_technical: The <svg> element is used as meaningful content but lacks role="img" and an accessible name (title + aria-labelledby or aria-label), violating WCAG 2.2 SC 1.1.1 (Non-text Content).
issues.why_simple: A screen reader user cannot understand what this SVG represents because it has no accessible name.
issues.why_technical: Screen readers treat SVG elements as images only when they have role="img" and an accessible name; without these, the SVG content is not exposed to assistive technology. NVDA + Firefox: skips the SVG entirely; JAWS 2024: does not announce the SVG as an image; VoiceOver iOS: ignores the SVG in swipe navigation.
issues.suggestion_technical: Add role="img" and aria-label="<descriptive text>" to the <svg> element, or include a <title> child element with an id and reference it via aria-labelledby.
